name: Corvus-Anvil
description: Corvus-Anvil is a hammerhead of dark stone adrift at the belt's outer lip, its leading hemisphere crater-glazed from eons of infall, its trailing face carved into long wind-cut flutes by solar wind that never stops blowing. The sky is black and crowded: belt debris drifts overhead in a frozen gray river, close enough to read a hull plate by reflected starlight.

Silence on the surface is total and structural—you feel it as pressure, the way you feel depth. The terminator is knife-edged, sunside rock hot enough to blister gloves, shadow cold enough to crack them, and every footstep throws dust that falls too fast, pulled down by a gravity denser than the moonlet's size should allow.

The distress beacon on the northern plain has transmitted for forty-one years—longer than any registered vessel of matching signature has been missing. Its signal is clean, its power supply unfathomable, and its message, when decoded, is not a call for help but a set of orbital elements describing an approach vector to Corvus-Anvil itself. Nine ships have followed it in. None have filed departure plans.

Titanium and copper lodes vein the crater walls thick enough to mine with bulldozers, and the claim auction is scheduled for spring. Prospecting drones keep losing signal over the beacon's coordinates, always at the same altitude, and the last two survey crews resigned within days of arrival—both citing the same observation: fresh bootprints around the beacon, no ship on any scanner.
